starting_points.name: Packaged uv application for maintained automation or a worker
starting_points.when: Reusable modules, a CLI entry point, tests or a long-lived worker warrant a maintained project.
steps: Install uv and inspect uv --version and uv init --help. Replace /path/to/local/source with an existing local source parent; use a new, absent target directory. Set PYTHON_VERSION to a supported Python minor compatible with the selected framework and dependencies. Record generator versions, selected flags and deliberate deviations.
Generate the packaged application, retain its importable src/worker_app package and generated console entry point, and replace the sample behavior with the bounded task or worker.

Install only required SDKs and configure tests, explicit inputs, credentials, timeouts and restart/checkpoint behavior. A Python project generator does not provision a queue, scheduler or orchestration service.

commands.purpose: Generate a packaged application and console entry point, explicitly selecting packaging across uv versions.
Resolve the project lock/environment and install the generated package.
Smoke-test the generated console entry point before adapting it to application behavior.

notes: Use --lib instead when the actual deliverable is a distributable library consumed by other projects. Do not choose library semantics solely because the code contains reusable functions.
The generic package generator supplies structure, not Celery tasks, Temporal workflows or safe retry semantics. Add the chosen worker integration only when required.
Choose a source parent outside another uv workspace, or intentionally use --no-workspace for an independent project under parent project metadata.

starting_points.name: Standalone script with inline dependency metadata
starting_points.when: A small, independently executable file is the actual deliverable; promote shared logic to a package when it grows.
steps: Install uv, choose a supported Python minor, and set PYTHON_VERSION accordingly. Use an existing local script folder and a new task.py; replace /path/to/local/scripts with that folder.
Generate the script, add only its required dependencies, implement the task, and create its adjacent lockfile for reproducible execution.

commands.purpose: Generate a standalone Python script with inline metadata.
Example only when HTTPX is required: declare a script dependency in its metadata.
Generate task.py.lock; standalone scripts do not use a project uv.lock.
Execute the script with its declared and locked dependencies after fixture-safe implementation.

notes: The HTTPX dependency is conditional. A standard-library-only script needs no extra package. Inline script metadata owns script dependencies; do not add a redundant pyproject.toml merely to run one file.

Keep task.py.lock with the script when reproducibility is required. For execution within a surrounding uv project, inspect project discovery and choose --no-project when the script should be independent.

follow_up_generators.name: Conditional Alembic migration environment and revisions
follow_up_generators.when: SQLAlchemy-backed persistent state is required; skip for stateless APIs/workers and preserve an existing migration owner.

commands.purpose: Install the selected PostgreSQL data dependencies; use a compatible driver for another chosen database.
Generate the standard migration environment and config.
After configuring env.py metadata and database access, generate a candidate schema revision.
After manual review, apply the candidate migration to a disposable development database.

notes: Between init and revision, configure the database URL from environment-owned secrets and target_metadata from the application models. The default generic template is synchronous; use alembic list_templates and choose the async template only for an actual async DBAPI.
Autogeneration cannot reliably infer every rename, constraint or data transformation. Review upgrade/downgrade operations and write data migrations intentionally; do not blindly apply its output.
Commit migrations, env.py and the non-secret configuration, while keeping database credentials out of source. Verify upgrades and required rollback behavior before release.

preserve: Keep generator-created project metadata, Python requirements, version selection and ignore rules; extend them rather than replacing them with a handwritten approximation.
Commit the resolved uv.lock for projects; exclude .venv, caches, secrets and platform debris such as .DS_Store. Do not hand-edit lockfiles.
Keep source repositories, virtual environments and caches in a local development workspace outside cloud-synced document folders.
For the packaged application, retain its generated build backend, src layout and console-script mapping; resolve dependency changes through uv.
For standalone scripts, preserve inline metadata and the adjacent task.py.lock rather than substituting a project uv.lock.
Keep fixtures and dry-run modes separate from live side effects; document scheduling, non-overlap and failure-resume behavior before operational use.
verification: For the packaged branch, from /path/to/local/source/worker-app run uv sync --locked and uv run worker-app using fixtures or an implemented dry-run mode; verify the packaged import and entry point after build/install when distributing.
For the script branch, from /path/to/local/scripts run uv run --locked task.py in a fixture-safe mode; verify its adjacent lockfile and Python requirement.
Run configured lint/type/test checks, then test explicit exit codes, malformed inputs, cancellation, bounded retries and partial failures at real effect boundaries.

Compare the same uv-version/flag scaffold in a disposable folder; inspect tracked/staged files for environments, caches, secrets and .DS_Store. Conditional Alembic checks require a configured disposable database.

integration_steps: After completing the selected generated baseline, keep its package layout and console entry point for maintained workers. From that project root, run uv add httpx pydantic pydantic-settings only for required HTTP/validation/settings capabilities, and uv add --dev ruff mypy pytest for the configured checks.

For the standalone-file baseline, declare required dependencies with uv add --script task.py httpx pydantic rather than project uv add, then refresh task.py.lock using uv lock --script task.py. Skip unused dependencies and promote shared logic into a package when reuse warrants it.
Implement explicit inputs, a dry-run or fixture mode, bounded external calls, structured result/error output and credentials injected by the environment.

Only when shared persistent state is required, use the conditional SQLAlchemy/Alembic follow-up generators and reviewed migrations. For durable orchestration, add temporalio to the maintained project and implement workflows/activities plus a worker connected to a separately provisioned Temporal service.

Package the locked environment for the chosen scheduler or worker platform. Record startup, non-overlap, cancellation, retry, checkpoint and failure-resume behavior; verify fixture execution before live access.
